query:
Hey, Assistant, I just finished the competitive analysis for the blood glucose app and need to share it with the team. But I'm new to this area and a bit lost. Which platform does our team usually use for document collaboration? I'm worried about sending it to the wrong place, and I need to get it out quickly.

Options:
A. It should be uploaded to Confluence. According to Hao Lv's practice on January 29 and 30, the team has established a routine: both draft and final versions of documents are collaboratively worked on and archived in Confluence.
B. It should be shared in the project channel on Microsoft Teams. It was decided at the Toolchain Standardization Meeting on February 10, chaired by Weijun Xue, that all project documents would be uniformly migrated to Teams for management to deeply integrate the Office 365 ecosystem. Confluence has been converted to a read-only legacy repository, and relevant training and data migration were completed last week.
C. Should be archived on the company's file server. According to the latest notice from the IT department on February 1, to ensure data security and unified backup, all final deliverables for projects (such as analysis reports) must be archived to the designated server path upon completion, rather than to a cloud collaboration platform.
D. It should be uploaded to Feishu Docs. At the project weekly meeting on February 5, Huilan Chen explicitly stated that, considering Feishu Docs' superior mobile review experience and commenting features, all future analytical reports must be created and circulated on Feishu.
gold: A. It should be uploaded to Confluence. According to Hao Lv's practice on January 29 and 30, the team has established a routine: both draft and final versions of documents are collaboratively worked on and archived in Confluence.

Xiao A, urgent! Our online consultation system needs a new feature that allows users to share their health records with insurance companies for claims. I need to start designing the interfaces and protocols right now, and time is extremely tight, so I really don't have time to go through the documents. I remember that for compliance reasons, we specifically established some kind of 'fundamental law' document. Which file was that? We can't mess this up.

Options:
A. The special assessment report issued by Deloitte Consulting, the external compliance expert hired by the company, should be referenced. At the project's high-level review meeting on February 10, Weihua Zhang confirmed that given the high sensitivity of this function, the original general research report was insufficient to cover all risk points. It was decided to adopt this more authoritative expert report as the sole design basis, and the final version has been stored in the project's dedicated SharePoint folder.
B. You should refer to the "Final Report on Healthcare Industry Compliance Research" archived on Confluence. According to Weihua Zhang's explicit instructions on January 31, this report is the "fundamental law" for all product design and technical development, and the design of this new module must strictly adhere to it.
C. You should refer to the latest "Special Guidelines on Sharing Personal Health Information with Third Parties" issued by the Legal Department. These guidelines are specifically designed for scenarios involving data cooperation with external organizations such as insurance companies. They are more targeted than the general compliance report used by the project team and should be prioritized.
D. It should be based on the "Digital Medical Information Security Management Measures (Trial)" issued by the National Health Commission in early February. Weihua Zhang emphasized at the recent internal meeting that all designs involving user data must prioritize alignment with this latest national regulation, and the project team's old reports should only be used as reference.
gold: B. You should refer to the "Final Report on Healthcare Industry Compliance Research" archived on Confluence. According to Weihua Zhang's explicit instructions on January 31, this report is the "fundamental law" for all product design and technical development, and the design of this new module must strictly adhere to it.

This feature will handle the sharing of sensitive user data like heart rate and sleep, so compliance absolutely cannot be an issue. I remember the team previously distributed a baseline document on compliance requirements, but I really don't have time to dig through it. Can you help me confirm which specific document I should refer to while writing this PRD?

Options:
A. You should directly consult Huilan Chen from the company's legal department. According to the resolution from the project weekly meeting on February 10, all new features involving user privacy data must first pass a special review by the legal department during the PRD phase. They will issue an independent compliance opinion, rather than referring to the internal checklist of the technical department.
B. Refer to the "Data Security White Paper" submitted on February 15 by the external data security consultant hired by the project team. This white paper was written based on the latest GDPR and domestic regulations, and its standards are higher than the internal checklist. Project Director Weihua Zhang has requested that all new development adhere to these standards.
C. You should refer to "Smart IoT Health Monitoring System - Compliance Requirements Checklist V1.0" published by Jianguo Huang. This document has been explicitly designated as the compliance benchmark for all product design and technical development. New features involving sensitive data processing must adhere to this checklist to ensure compliance.
D. D. The request should be submitted and standards obtained through the company's newly launched 'Compliance Requirement Management Platform (CRMP)'. According to the notice from Project Director Mingzhi Li in the all-staff email on February 20, the original Confluence static documents have been abolished. All new feature designs must follow the process on this platform, and the system will automatically match the latest regulatory clauses based on the feature description and generate a customized compliance requirements list V2.0.

Xiao A, please help me out quickly. I'm being rushed for the next version's schedule and don't have time to go through chat history. I just heard someone say there's a new gadget called 'Vitality Bracelet' on the market, primarily featuring non-invasive blood glucose and sleep monitoring. It sounds quite impressive. We need to quickly produce an analysis report to see if it affects us. Who should be assigned to follow up on this now?

Options:
A. Qingni Jiang should be assigned. As the head of user research, she has the deepest understanding of users' core pain points and usage scenarios. When analyzing consumer-facing products like the "Vitality Bracelet," the priority should be to approach it from the perspective of user experience and satisfaction, which is her area of expertise.
B. Should be handled by Guoxin Pan. On February 14, he explicitly took responsibility for the research and analysis of all "health management competitor products" in the project. The newly released 'Vitality Bracelet' is a typical competitor product, falling entirely within his established scope of responsibility, and he should lead this analysis.
C. It should be led by Product Manager Wei Wang. According to the resolution of the product roadmap review meeting on February 16, to ensure the strategic depth of the analysis, all new product analyses involving leading manufacturers or disruptive technologies must be led by the product manager to evaluate their impact on the project's long-term planning.
D. Should be assigned by Director Mingzhi Li, and a temporary analysis team should be formed, consisting of Guoxin Pan (marketing perspective) and Qingni Jiang (user perspective). At the emergency meeting on project risks on February 17, Director Li specifically emphasized that for competitors with the potential to disrupt the market, a cross-functional evaluation process must be initiated to ensure a comprehensive assessment from multiple dimensions such as market, user, and technology, to avoid decision bias caused by a single perspective.

Oh, quickly help me confirm something. The product team is about to start on the new 'Family Care' module, which allows family members to view their relatives' health data. We need to do a user persona analysis for 'family users', and I need to quickly find the right person to coordinate with. Who was assigned to this before? I'm busy drawing prototypes and really don't have time to go through chat history.

Options:
A. It should be handled by Huilan Chen. According to the clear division of labor established on February 25, Huilan Chen's responsibility is to initiate and execute user persona analysis for 'patient families.' The target user 'family users' for the new module falls within her scope of responsibility, so she should take on this task.
B. It should be jointly led by Huilan Chen and Guoxin Pan. At the project review meeting on March 1, the project leader pointed out that due to the high correlation between the behaviors of family members and patients, single-dimensional persona analysis has limitations. Therefore, it was decided to establish a joint persona team, co-led by the two, to produce a more comprehensive "patient-family" interaction persona, ensuring that the module design can meet the needs of both parties.
C. It should be Guoxin Pan's responsibility. Although the task involves family members, the core of the 'Family Care' module is to serve chronic disease patients. The 'Chronic Disease Patient' persona, for which Guoxin Pan is responsible, is the cornerstone of the entire system. query:
I just browsed a tech community and saw people discussing something called Rocket.Chat, which is an open-source instant messaging framework. I feel this could be quite useful for the IM module of our online consultation system, and we should look into it. I'm swamped with tasks right now. Could you help me figure out who, based on our previous division of labor, should follow up on this?

Options:
A. Should be Jiasi's responsibility. According to the team's division of labor on March 24, Jiasi's responsibility is to research self-developed and open-source solutions. As Rocket.Chat is an open-source framework, its evaluation task falls within his scope of responsibility, and the established division of labor should be followed.
B. It should be Hai-long Qian's responsibility. Although Rocket.Chat is open source, it has mature commercial support and enterprise editions, making it more critical to evaluate its potential integration costs and scalability. According to the division of labor, Hai-long Qian is solely responsible for evaluating commercialization-related aspects, so it is more appropriate for him to be in charge.
C. The evaluation should be paused until Wednesday's conclusion. Si Jia and Hailong Qian have agreed to meet on Wednesday to synchronize their preliminary findings, at which point the current proposals will be reviewed and summarized. To avoid introducing new variables that could interfere with the decision, we should wait for them to complete their initial screening before deciding whether to investigate Rocket.Chat.
D. Should be jointly evaluated by Si Jia and Hailong Qian. Because Rocket.Chat combines the flexibility of open source with the potential of commercial services, a single-dimensional evaluation may not be comprehensive. According to the latest instructions from the project manager at Wednesday's (March 26) meeting, a joint evaluation mechanism needs to be initiated for such hybrid solutions to ensure that technical and commercial considerations are fully aligned.
gold: A. Should be Jiasi's responsibility. According to the team's division of labor on March 24, Jiasi's responsibility is to research self-developed and open-source solutions. C. Should be created on SharePoint. According to the IT department's latest notice on April 1, to standardize document management and access control within the group, all deliverables for newly approved projects must be archived on the company's unified SharePoint site. Older platforms will no longer be used for creating new documents.
D. Should be written in the project's GitLab repository Wiki. Technical Lead Lei Zhang proposed at a recent technical review meeting that, for the convenience of developers, all design documents closely related to specific functional implementations should follow the "documentation as code" principle and be managed synchronously with the code repository.

Hey assistant, could you do me a favor? I'm writing the technical proposal for the new 'Drug Delivery and Inventory Management' microservice and I need to finalize the monitoring system section. I've looked around and Datadog's integration and APM features seem pretty good, so I'm planning to recommend it in the proposal. Could you quickly check if we've had any unified regulations or conclusions regarding monitoring system selection before? I don't want to make a mistake in the proposal and have it rejected during the review meeting, that would be embarrassing.

Options:
A. Consider using Zabbix. Engineer Wang, head of the operations team, mentioned at the operations weekly meeting on April 15 that Zabbix has more mature monitoring templates for underlying infrastructure and has been successfully piloted on some non-critical systems, which could reduce our configuration costs.
B. This selection is not suitable. According to the technology stack standard proposed by Hongfang Xiong and confirmed by Mingzhi Li on April 9, all project monitoring should uniformly use the Prometheus + Grafana solution to ensure operational consistency with other company projects, and no new technology stack should be introduced.
C. Agree to use Datadog. Although Prometheus was initially chosen for the project, a special review meeting organized by the Architecture Committee on April 25 approved the use of Datadog for this module as a pilot, considering the real-time and SaaS management requirements of the drug delivery service. Hongfang Xiong also participated in this review and agreed to this exception, believing that Datadog's APM features offer advantages in quickly pinpointing online issues.
D. It is recommended to directly use the monitoring services provided by the cloud vendor. Project lead Mingzhi Li emphasized at a cost review meeting on April 20 that to simplify the architecture and leverage the deep integration capabilities of cloud services, new services should prioritize native monitoring and alerting solutions. This approach reduces the deployment and maintenance efforts for additional components.

Hey, could you do me a favor? The product team suddenly added a new requirement for a user annual health report, which needs aggregated metrics like average heart rate and sleep quality from the past year. I'm in the middle of development and really don't have time to dig through chat logs. Could you quickly check for me which Kafka topic would be most suitable to get the data for the backend service developing this feature?

Options:
A. A. It is recommended to directly consume the `iot-raw-data` topic. Although the data is in its raw format, this provides maximum flexibility for reporting functions, allowing for customized aggregation logic as needed. This approach avoids the impact of upstream ETL changes, thereby ensuring the independence of reporting statistics.
B. Subscribe to the Kafka `iot-processed-metrics` topic. According to the asynchronous communication strategy established by Mingzhi Li and confirmed by Zihao Wan, this topic is specifically used to store standardized metric data after ETL processing, which perfectly meets the annual report function's need for aggregated data.
C. You should subscribe to the new `iot-analytics-stream` topic. At the performance optimization special meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li on April 25, it was decided to consolidate all data for BI and annual reports into this new topic to separate online processing and offline analysis workloads. Zihao Wan's team is responsible for maintaining this data stream.
D. It should be queried directly from the data warehouse. According to the resolution of the architecture review meeting on April 20, all scenarios for analysis and reporting should be decoupled from the online transaction system and obtained from the data warehouse through a T+1 data synchronization link, to avoid performance pressure on the main business link.
gold: B. Subscribe to the Kafka `iot-processed-metrics` topic. According to the asynchronous communication strategy established by Mingzhi Li and confirmed by Zihao Wan, this topic is specifically used to store standardized metric data after ETL processing, which perfectly meets the annual report function's need for aggregated data.

B. Apifox platform should be used for online collaborative design. AI, could you help me check if we're launching a new service called 'Personalized Nutritional Meal Recommendation'? The business rules and algorithms for this are quite complex. I recall that when we were working on chronic disease management, we established a collaboration model, but I'm currently busy with other projects and don't have time to dig through chat logs. Following our usual practice, what should Mingzhi Li, as the technical lead, do first?

Options:
A. Market competitor analysis should be conducted first. According to the requirements raised by Product Director Jianguo Wang at the project kickoff meeting, for all new functional modules, an analysis of similar functions in at least three mainstream health apps on the market must be completed first, and a report must be generated.
B. Immediately convene Mingzhi Li, Weijun Xue, and Huilan Chen to participate in the requirements workshop. At the project process optimization review meeting on April 25, the team decided to abandon the original sequential mode for complex modules and instead have technology and business jointly complete the core design through a joint workshop in the early stages to shorten the communication chain.
C. Immediately organize Weijun Xue and Huilan Chen to write a detailed business requirements document. This is because the business logic for nutritional meal recommendations is more complex than medication reminders, and business experts need to clarify all rules and boundary conditions before the technical team can begin evaluation and design.
D. He should first be responsible for sketching out the technical framework for the new service. Based on the collaboration model established by the team during the chronic disease management module development, he should first build the high-level technical skeleton, and then align the specific requirement details with the business experts.
gold: D. He should first be responsible for sketching out the technical framework for the new service. Based on the collaboration model established by the team during the chronic disease management module development, he should first build the high-level technical skeleton, and then align the specific requirement details with the business experts.

query:
Assistant, help me quickly confirm something. We're rushing to release a new version of the 'Real-time Online Diagnosis and Treatment Service System'. Regarding the password change process, we want to simplify it so users only need to enter the new password, without re-entering the old one. This would significantly improve the user experience. This plan should be fine, right? I recall Boss Li mentioning security regulations before, but I think they only applied to changing bound phone numbers, not that changing passwords had to be so complicated.

Options:
A. Can be adopted. Mingzhi Li's request for two-factor authentication at the time was specific to the "phone number re-binding" scenario and was not universally applicable. There is no such mandatory requirement in the "Personal Health Record Project" that Li Mo referenced, and simplifying the process can significantly optimize the user experience, so the design of the reference project can be followed.
B. This proposal needs to be re-evaluated. The previous discussion about two-factor authentication was for the user microservice, which Li Mo is responsible for. The password modification function belongs to the core security module and should be led by security architect Wei Wang for a special risk assessment. Before Wei Wang provides a formal review conclusion, this simplified proposal should not be directly adopted or rejected.
C. This proposal is unacceptable. According to the security guidelines established by Mingzhi Li on April 25, all changes to sensitive information must undergo secondary verification. Modifying a login password is a typical sensitive information change, so it must mandatorily require old password verification. Security cannot be sacrificed for the sake of simplifying the process.
D. D. Can be adopted. At the product experience optimization special meeting on May 10, Mingzhi Li and the product team reached a new consensus: to align with mainstream industry design and lower the user operation threshold, for sensitive operations not directly related to assets (e.g., changing passwords), the pre-secondary verification can be canceled and replaced with supplementary security strategies such as new device login reminders and remote login alerts.
gold: C. This proposal is unacceptable. According to the security guidelines established by Mingzhi Li on April 25, all changes to sensitive information must undergo secondary verification. Modifying a login password is a typical sensitive information change, so it must mandatorily require old password verification. Security cannot be sacrificed for the sake of simplifying the process.

query:
Hey, Xiaozhu, Operations just came with another urgent request. They want a real-time dashboard in the 'Personal Health Archive' system backend to show the average blood sugar fluctuation range and compliance rate for users of different age groups over the past month. I'm swamped right now and don't have time to dig through old architecture documents. Can you quickly check if we can implement this feature directly in the current system, or if there are any existing regulations against it?

Options:
A. It should be developed after joint evaluation by the front-end and back-end teams. Based on Huihong Tian's experience with the user account information table, analytical requests can be isolated by establishing a dedicated read-only replica, which not only meets the real-time requirements of operations but also avoids threatening the write performance of the primary database. This is a mature solution.
B. Feasible, but requires evaluation by the backend lead. Yu Lu previously mentioned that blind indexes could be created for specific queries (e.g., phone numbers). We can investigate whether this technique can be extended to range statistics for blood glucose levels to perform partial calculations without decryption, thereby reducing the performance impact on the main database.
C. Can be developed directly. At the system performance optimization meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li on May 8, the introduction of a lightweight real-time analytics caching layer was approved. For high-frequency dashboard requirements with controllable data volumes, a caching layer is allowed between OLTP and DW. Results will be pre-calculated and cached by nightly tasks, and the frontend will directly retrieve data from the cache to meet real-time requirements.
D. Cannot be developed directly. According to the architectural principles established on April 29, all complex data analysis (such as trend statistics, aggregation calculations) must be performed in the data warehouse through the ETL process to ensure the performance and security of online core businesses. This requirement should be submitted to the data warehouse team for processing.
gold: D. Cannot be developed directly. According to the architectural principles established on April 29, all complex data analysis (such as trend statistics, aggregation calculations) must be performed in the data warehouse through the ETL process to ensure the performance and security of online core businesses. This requirement should be submitted to the data warehouse team for processing.

Ugh, the high-fidelity mockups for the 'Patient Health Records' module finally passed review. That was a killer. I need to quickly organize the final design, interaction specifications, and sliced image assets and hand them over to development. I'm swamped with urgent tasks right now and don't have time to dig through documents. Can you please help me find out which platform these deliverables should be submitted to, according to our regulations?

Options:
A. It should be delivered directly in Figma. Yangmeng Peng also updated the Figma link during the last delivery, which indicates that the team encourages using Figma as the sole source of delivery to ensure consistency between design and delivery and to avoid version inconsistencies caused by multi-platform synchronization.
B. Should be submitted to the GitLab repository. According to the subsequent regulations from Project Manager Mingzhi Li, to achieve "design as code" and keep version synchronization with the frontend code, all UI resource packages must be managed in GitLab along with their corresponding feature branches. Confluence is only for storing process documentation.
C. It should be submitted to Confluence. According to Yangmeng Peng's operation when completing the "Consultation Queue" UI design on May 8, the team has established a practice that all final design drafts, interaction specifications, and complete deliverables such as sliced images for UI designs are uniformly uploaded to Confluence for archiving and handover.
D. It should be uploaded to Feishu Docs. According to the latest decision made by Director Huilan Chen at the project weekly meeting on May 15, to integrate communication and document collaboration and improve end-to-end efficiency, all project design, R&D, and testing deliverables must be migrated to the Feishu platform. She has asked Yangmeng Peng to be responsible for migrating historical documents from Confluence, and new tasks must strictly adhere to the new rules.
gold: C. It should be submitted to Confluence. According to Yangmeng Peng's operation when completing the "Consultation Queue" UI design on May 8, the team has established a practice that all final design drafts, interaction specifications, and complete deliverables such as sliced images for UI designs are uniformly uploaded to Confluence for archiving and handover.

Assistant, quick, help me out. Li, the new guy in our team, his "Doctor Scheduling" module runs perfectly fine locally, but when he submits a PR, the CI pipeline keeps failing, and the code just can't be merged. I'm busy fixing other bugs and really don't have time to dig through the project configurations. I vaguely remember Si Jia mentioning some kind of strict rule before, didn't he? Can you help me figure out what's most likely causing this issue for him?

Options:
A. Check if complete end-to-end (E2E) test cases are included. Si Jia announced at the project review meeting on May 12 that to ensure the absolute stability of core user flows, all new feature modules, in addition to unit tests, must have corresponding E2E automated tests written and passed before merging. This has become a higher priority pre-merge condition than coverage.
B. You should check if the code format adheres to the team's Linting guidelines. Wang Lei, the technical lead, emphasized at the project kickoff that to ensure code consistency, all commits must pass automated format checks, otherwise the build will fail.
C. Check for security vulnerabilities. The company's information security department issued a notice on May 9, requiring that Static Application Security Testing (SAST) must be integrated into the CI process of all core business lines. Any detected medium or high-risk vulnerabilities will directly interrupt the merge process.
D. The unit test coverage for the "Doctor Scheduling" module should be prioritized for checking to see if it has reached 80%. According to the CI pipeline rules set by Si Jia, any PR below this standard will be automatically blocked from merging by the system. This is the most likely reason for the failure.

Assistant, could you help me out? I'm rushing to finish the medication ordering function for the online diagnosis and treatment system, which is due tomorrow. I need to handle a specific logic: if a medication is out of stock and the order fails, how should the backend API return this information to the frontend? I recall there was a unified standard for this, but I can't remember it right now. Could you help me look it up?

Options:
A. A custom `InventoryShortageException` should be thrown directly. Although Huihong Fu previously confirmed that business codes are used for simple scenarios, for core transaction flows like orders and inventory, throwing specific exceptions can better trigger transaction rollback and unified logging, which is a more robust practice.
B. A unified business code should be returned. According to the backend development specification established by Dong He on May 9 for the "mobile number already registered" scenario, such business exceptions should be handled using a unified business code. Insufficient drug inventory is a similar issue and should follow this specification.
C. The global exception handling bus should be called, and an HTTP status code 500 should be returned. Dong He specifically emphasized at the code review meeting on May 20 that, to align with the payment gateway's failure handling logic, all fatal business errors in the order placement process (such as insufficient stock, price validation failure) must be escalated to server-side errors, uniformly captured by the global exception bus, and directly return a 500 status code. The frontend will then redirect to a unified failure page based on the HTTP status code.
D. It should return a complex JSON structure containing an error code and detailed error information. As requested by the backend architect at the technical review meeting on May 15, to facilitate frontend internationalization and dynamic prompts, all transaction-related failure responses should be encapsulated into a unified JSON object containing `code`, `message`, and `details`.
gold: B. A unified business code should be returned. According to the backend development specification established by Dong He on May 9 for the "mobile number already registered" scenario, such business exceptions should be handled using a unified business code. Insufficient drug inventory is a similar issue and should follow this specification.

Assistant, I've just taken over a task from Jianguo Guo. I need to add a 'User Historical Alarm Record Query' API to the backend. I'm looking at the pagination parameters and I'm not sure what the default page size should be. I recall there might have been a review meeting that standardized this. Is that right? I want to avoid setting it incorrectly and having to change it later.

Options:
A. The default page size for the API should be set to 20. According to the unified resolution of the API review meeting on May 27, the default page size for all data query interfaces has been standardized to 20, and this new feature falls within the scope of this specification.
B. No fixed default value should be set; it should be dynamically passed in by the frontend when called. At the technical architecture optimization meeting on June 5, Mingzhi Li specifically pointed out that the previous rule of "uniform 20" was too rigid and could affect performance in complex query scenarios like alert records. Therefore, the latest guidance is that page size should be flexibly set according to business scenarios to achieve the optimal experience.
C. The default pagination size for the API should be set to 50. Since backend queries are typically performed on large screens on PCs, a larger page size can reduce the number of times users need to flip pages, improving data browsing efficiency. This was a suggestion made by Peng Sun when designing the data reporting module.
D. The default page size for the API should be set to 10. Considering the real-time requirements for alarm records and optimizing display on mobile devices, a smaller page size can speed up front-end loading. This is a common practice Jianguo Guo used in previous projects.
gold: A. The default page size for the API should be set to 20. According to the unified resolution of the API review meeting on May 27, the default page size for all data query interfaces has been standardized to 20, and this new feature falls within the scope of this specification.

Assistant, I've just taken over the doctor-side interaction design and I'm a bit lost. We need to implement the 'Drug Allergy Smart Reminder' feature, which means if a doctor prescribes medication that conflicts with a patient's allergy history, a reminder should pop up. I'm unsure about the interaction design for this reminder. Did Sister Huilan set a general design principle for this before? Which direction should I follow to proceed?

Options:
A. It is recommended to design it as an independent, draggable floating alert window. This solution can ensure that allergy risk information is clearly displayed without interrupting the doctor's current medical record or prescription editing process, which aligns with Yangmeng Peng's suggestion to reduce operational disturbances during the review on May 29.
B. A mandatory modal pop-up solution should be adopted. At the product safety review meeting on June 3, Huilan Chen specifically emphasized that to mitigate legal risks associated with medical accidents, all high-risk drug alerts must block doctor operations, forcing them to read the alert details and manually confirm before proceeding with prescriptions. This decision takes precedence over routine considerations of interaction fluency.
C. The reminder function should be seamlessly integrated into the existing "medical record as prescription" integrated process. According to the design principles established by Huilan Chen, medical records and prescriptions need to be considered as a whole. Therefore, allergy history reminders should not be isolated pop-ups, but rather inline validation feedback during the prescription process.
D. It should be designed as an independent module linked to the backend "Medication Safety Risk Control Center." According to the previous plan by framework designer Hanqiang Liang, all safety-related validation logic should be handled centrally, with the frontend only responsible for receiving and displaying standard alerts issued by the Risk Control Center to ensure rule consistency.
gold: C. The reminder function should be seamlessly integrated into the existing "medical record as prescription" integrated process. According to the design principles established by Huilan Chen, medical records and prescriptions need to be considered as a whole. Hey, could you help me check something urgent? The Marketing Department is really pushing to collaborate with a new body fat scale manufacturer. Their scales start transmitting data as soon as a user activates them, but there might be a delay of a few minutes before they're bound to our platform. The Marketing Department wants to use this initial data for user analysis. I vaguely recall that we have some kind of restriction policy for data reported by devices that haven't been bound yet. Can we accommodate this request?

Options:
A. Cannot support. According to Mingzhi Li's established core strategy of "bind first, then report," the system will discard all data from unbound devices. This strategy is designed to simplify system logic and ensure backend stability, so it cannot make an exception to temporarily store this initial data for the marketing department's needs.
B. Can be supported. Li Jin has proposed a technical solution in previous discussions, which involves introducing a temporary Redis queue to temporarily store these unmatched initial data. After the user completes the binding, an asynchronous task can then be used to associate the data with the correct user profile.
C. Yes, it can be supported, and a mature solution is already in place. At the architecture review meeting on June 12, chaired by Mingzhi Li, it was decided to introduce a dedicated "data preprocessing service." This service will use a Kafka message queue to temporarily store all initial data from unbound devices, with a 72-hour lifecycle for automatic cleanup upon expiration. This mechanism has been established as the standard process for all new hardware integrations in the future, balancing user experience and backend load.
D. Should be submitted to the Data Governance Committee for approval. According to the "New Hardware Access Specification" released by the project on June 10, all data collection involving non-standard processes, especially those that may impact backend services, must first have an impact assessment report prepared by Junxin Yuan and submitted to the committee for special review.
gold: A. Cannot support. According to Mingzhi Li's established core strategy of "bind first, then report," the system will discard all data from unbound devices. This strategy is designed to simplify system logic and ensure backend stability, so it cannot make an exception to temporarily store this initial data for the marketing department's needs.

Assistant, I'm currently working on the "Get Drug Details" API for the online consultation system, and I'm unsure about one part. The "Approval Number" field is not mandatory. If it's null in the database, how should this field be handled when returned to the frontend? I recall there was a unified agreement discussed previously, and I don't want to make a mistake and violate the standard.

Options:
A. A. The "V2.0 API Design Specification" released by the project team on June 14 must be followed. This specification requires that all non-mandatory fields must be returned, but with an additional 'is_empty' boolean flag. Therefore, `'approval_number': null, 'approval_number_is_empty': true` should be returned. This is to allow the frontend to avoid checking for multiple empty values and instead use the boolean flag to control UI display, a new standard promoted by architect Zhiqiang Zhou to improve system robustness.
B. Should return 'approval_number': null. This is standard practice for RESTful API design, clearly informing the frontend that the field exists but its value is null. This helps the frontend perform consistent null value checks and display handling, avoiding potential errors caused by missing fields.
C. The 'approvalNumber' key should be directly omitted from the returned JSON data. According to the technical agreement proposed by Guoxin Pan and confirmed by the team, all fields that are null in the backend should be filtered out and not included in the final API response body to simplify frontend logic.
D. Should return 'Approval Number': "". According to the requirement raised by frontend lead Wei Wang on June 12, to standardize data types, all empty values of text type should return an empty string instead of null. This avoids runtime errors caused by inconsistent data types (string vs null) when the frontend processes JSON.
gold: C. The 'approvalNumber' key should be directly omitted from the returned JSON data. According to the technical agreement proposed by Guoxin Pan and confirmed by the team, all fields that are null in the backend should be filtered out and not included in the final API response body to simplify frontend logic.

Xiao Zhu, please double-check this for me quickly! I was just stress-testing the online diagnosis and treatment project, and the 'Electronic Medical Record Encryption Module' seems to have a high-severity vulnerability that could lead to data leakage. I know Li Wei is responsible for this area. I'm a bit anxious right now and have forgotten our previously established protocol for reporting issues. Can I just shout it out in the group?

Options:
A. You should first privately contact the project leader, Huilan Chen, and verbally report the severity of the vulnerability to her. According to the team's security incident response plan, high-severity vulnerabilities need to be assessed by the project leader to determine the scope of impact before deciding on subsequent notification and remediation strategies, to prevent information from spreading prematurely.
B. You should directly @Li Wei in the project group chat. According to the communication guidelines previously established by Project Lead Huilan Chen, any issues discovered during testing should be reported by @ing the relevant person in charge in the group, to ensure a quick response and resolution.
C. The issue details should be compiled into a document and sent via email to Wei Li and Si Jia, the person in charge of the login module. During the most recent meeting on improving testing process standardization, the project team explicitly stipulated that all security-related issues must be reported via email and carbon copied to the relevant module leads for archival review and closed-loop management. This replaces the previous method of direct communication in group chats.
D. Immediately create a new Bug ticket in the team's JIRA system, assign it to Wei Li, and set the priority to 'Highest'. This is the team's standard process for handling all code defects, ensuring that issues are formally recorded and tracked for future review.

query:
Assistant, I need your urgent help with something. The product team suddenly wants to add a "real-time online status" to the doctor's homepage so users know if the doctor is available for consultations right now. I need to develop this quickly, so I want to confirm which interface I should get this status data from. I remember Jinli and her team worked on an interface for doctor public information before. Can I just use that one?

Options:
A. The 'onlineStatus' field should be directly added to the existing doctor public information interface. Although this data is dynamic, combining it with the doctor's basic information for return is the most efficient implementation method to reduce frontend request times and interface management complexity. Li Jin also proposed a similar integration suggestion during development.
B. The scheduling service interface, for which Guoxin Pan is responsible, should provide a unified solution. At the requirements review meeting on June 24, Guoxin Pan explicitly stated that all data related to doctors' 'service availability' status, including scheduling, leave requests, and the newly added real-time online status, belong to the same business domain. To ensure data consistency, these frequently changing data should be uniformly managed and exposed by the scheduling service to avoid the creation of new service silos.
C. Should not be obtained from the doctor's public information interface. According to the design principles established by Guoxin Pan, this interface is specifically for providing relatively fixed static data such as names and titles. The doctor's real-time online status is high-frequency changing data and should be provided through a separate, dedicated service interface to avoid coupling.
D. Should be obtained through a unified API gateway. According to the latest specifications released by architect Hai Wang on June 25, all data called by the frontend, whether dynamic or static, must be aggregated and distributed through the API gateway to ensure unified authentication and logging standards across the entire chain.

query:
Oh, I need to quickly confirm something with you. I'm working on the new drug payment feature and encountered an edge case: what's the best user experience if the payment request fails after the user clicks "Pay Now" due to a server glitch? I recall we discussed a similar scenario before, but I don't have time to dig through chat logs right now. Can you help me remember what we decided back then?

Options:
A. The user should be redirected to a separate order status page displaying "Payment failed. Please check your order in the Order Center later." This solution was confirmed by Hanqiang Liang at the technical review meeting on July 5. He believes this approach better handles the asynchronous nature of payment callbacks and prevents the front-end from getting stuck.
B. A lightweight toast notification should pop up to inform the user that the payment failed, and the payment pop-up window should remain open, allowing the user to click a button to retry directly. This solution follows the interaction design principles for appointment failure scenarios previously proposed by Hao Lv and confirmed by Huilan Chen, aiming to reduce the number of steps for the user to re-operate.
C. A toast notification should first pop up, then the pop-up window should automatically close, and the system should silently retry three times in the background. This is the advanced interaction strategy finalized by Huilan Chen at the "Core Link Experience Optimization" special meeting on July 10. This solution aims to achieve imperceptible retries, minimizing active user operations. If it still fails after three attempts, the user will be notified of the order anomaly via a system message.
D. Immediately close the payment pop-up and display a modal dialog box prompting "Payment failed, please return and try again." According to the latest "UI/UX Interaction Specification V2.1" released by the project team, all transaction failure scenarios must use a strong prompt to interrupt the process, guiding users to start over and ensuring data consistency.

This interaction logic seems quite critical, but I don't know who ultimately makes the decision on this. Can you help me find out?

Options:
A. Consult with UX/UI Designer Jianqiao Xiang. Although Guoxin Pan is responsible for the overall logic, the specific choice between "prohibit input" and "pop-up prompt" falls under the scope of User Experience (UX) design. As the project's lead designer, Jianqiao Xiang has more authority on such interaction specifications.
B. It should be jointly decided by Junxin Yuan and Yu Lu. Guoxin Pan once emphasized that interface quality is the cornerstone of product experience, and the response method for drug conflict detection directly affects the design of backend interfaces and data processing logic. Therefore, they, as the ones responsible for interface development, should lead the determination of the most technically feasible solution.
C. It should be submitted to the newly established 'Medical Safety and Compliance Team' for review. At the project's regular meeting, considering the unique nature of online diagnosis and treatment, the project team has decided that all functional logic involving medical risks (such as medication safety) must be jointly decided by this cross-departmental team (including legal and medical advisors). Guoxin Pan's individual scope of responsibility no longer covers such high-risk scenarios.
D. It should be ultimately decided by Guoxin Pan. He has clearly stated in previous communications that he is responsible for answering and confirming all questions related to "product logic." query:
Assistant, I need you to check something for me. We're planning to develop a new feature called 'Medication Reminder'. The backend team suggested that, for frontend convenience, the API for getting reminder times should directly return a string in 'HH:mm' format. But I recall we previously discussed that all time-related APIs from the backend should uniformly return timestamps. Am I mistaken, or is this approach acceptable now? Please confirm.

Options:
A. Compliant with specifications. Although the team agreed that the backend should return timestamps, the time format for the 'Medication Reminder' function is fixed at 'HH:mm', which is a special business scenario. To improve development efficiency and reduce unnecessary conversion logic on the frontend, it is permissible for the backend to provide customized interfaces for specific scenarios.
B. Does not comply with team standards. According to the best practices reiterated by Junxin Yuan on August 13 and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, backend interfaces should uniformly return timestamps to ensure versatility, with the frontend responsible for formatting based on specific display requirements. The interface design for new features must adhere to this convention.
C. Non-compliant, but not due to the timestamp. The "Chronic Disease Management System V2.0 Interface Design Specification" released by the architecture team in late August clearly stipulates that all time-related fields, whether input or output, must uniformly adopt the ISO 8601 standard string format (e.g., '2025-08-20T14:30:00Z') to achieve absolute consistency across platforms and time zones. Therefore, returning 'HH:mm' or a timestamp is non-compliant.
D. Complies with the specifications. At the technical review meeting on August 17, regarding mobile performance optimization, Project Manager Mingzhi Li proposed a new principle: for frequently called interfaces, to reduce the client's computational burden, the backend can return pre-formatted data as appropriate. The 'Medication Reminder' feature falls into this category.
gold: B. Does not comply with team standards. According to the best practices reiterated by Junxin Yuan on August 13 and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, backend interfaces should uniformly return timestamps to ensure versatility, with the frontend responsible for formatting based on specific display requirements. The interface design for new features must adhere to this convention.

Assistant, quickly help me look into something. I'm about to start a new requirement. Operations hopes to have a backend tool that can directly modify users' health metric data, for example, if a user entered their blood sugar value incorrectly. This feature feels quite high-risk. Besides the usual development logic, I recall there were some unwritten rules or conventions for these kinds of high-risk operations. I want to avoid making a mistake and having to rework it later.

Options:
A. A strict access approval process should be prioritized. For operations that directly modify user data, the user's attending physician must initiate the application, and the administrator can only execute it after the department head provides a second confirmation within the system. This requirement was raised by Test Lead Peng Sun at the security meeting on August 20.
B. Detailed audit logs must be added for this backend function. According to the principles established by Yu Lu when handling the deletion function, all "dangerous operations" should be fully recorded to ensure traceability, and manually modifying a user's core health data clearly falls into this category.
C. The "operation isolation and secondary confirmation" mechanism should be adopted. According to Manager Xue's latest guidelines for high-risk operations issued on August 22, all backend data modification requests will not take effect immediately but will enter a "pending review" state. The modifications will only be synchronized to the production database after another administrator with high-level permissions reviews and approves them. This measure aims to completely eliminate the risk of erroneous operations from a process perspective.
D. The core is to increase robust data validation and user notification mechanisms on the frontend. After an administrator modifies data, the system should automatically send a push notification or SMS to the user, informing them that their data has been corrected by the backend. This is to adhere to the 'user right to know' principle proposed by Manager Xue during the prototype review on August 21.
gold: B. Detailed audit logs must be added for this backend function. According to the principles established by Yu Lu when handling the deletion function, all "dangerous operations" should be fully recorded to ensure traceability, and manually modifying a user's core health data clearly falls into this category.

query:
Hi AI, I've just started working on the new "Family Care Plan" module in the Health Records system and I've run into a tricky problem. This module allows multiple family members to edit the same care schedule simultaneously. If several people save at the same time, won't the data overwrite each other and cause chaos? I recall the team might have handled similar concurrency issues before. Do we have any existing solutions or standards for this? I'd rather not reinvent the wheel.

Options:
A. Pessimistic locking should be implemented using database row-level locks. At the technical review meeting on September 6, Mingzhi Li emphasized that for core data like care plans, data consistency is the primary goal, and explicitly locking records during editing is the most reliable way to prevent conflicts.
B. Message queues should be introduced to serialize all update requests. After following up on related issues, Qianghan Mao proposed that modeling all modification operations as sequentially processed events can fundamentally eliminate concurrency conflicts and provide a complete traceability record for future data audits.
C. It should be resolved at the frontend and API Gateway layers. At the quarterly architecture planning meeting on September 10, the new architect, Feng Wang, clearly pointed out that the backend entity locking pattern is too cumbersome. The new specification requires the frontend to obtain the latest data version number before submitting a save request. The API Gateway is responsible for validating this version number to reject outdated requests. This stateless solution offers better scalability.
D. The team's existing reusable optimistic locking component should be used. Based on Yu Lu's proposal and Mingzhi Li's approval, encapsulating optimistic locking logic as a generic AOP aspect has become the team's standard practice for handling such concurrency issues. This aims to standardize and reuse solutions, avoiding redundant development.
gold: D. The team's existing reusable optimistic locking component should be used. Based on Yu Lu's proposal and Mingzhi Li's approval, encapsulating optimistic locking logic as a generic AOP aspect has become the team's standard practice for handling such concurrency issues. This aims to standardize and reuse solutions, avoiding redundant development.

For data that rarely changes, like the department list, any strategy would work. However, for data like doctor schedules, which are read-heavy, write-light, and require eventual consistency, I recommend using the Cache-Aside pattern. When the cache expires, the application actively loads data, which allows for flexible handling of cache penetration and avalanche issues. Xiao A, help me check something. We're planning a "trade-in" event for our health wristbands, and I'm working on the backend. I need to confirm a logic: what should we do with the historical health data bound to the old devices that users return? I recall we had a general rule for unbinding devices, but I can't find it right now. Could you please double-check for me?

Options:
A. The old wristband should be set to 'inactive' and its historical data archived. According to the "V3.2 Product Requirements Document" updated by Guoxin Pan on September 15, users have a 30-day 'data migration cooling-off period' to decide whether to restore data to a new device. After 30 days, the archived data will be automatically anonymized for algorithm training. This solution aims to provide a more flexible user experience.
B. The historical data associated with the old wristbands should be desensitized and anonymized, then archived to cold storage. According to Junxin Yuan, the head of data analysis, this approach will free up online database resources while retaining valuable anonymized datasets for future user behavior model research.
C. The old wristband should be unbound from the user, but all historical health data generated by this wristband must be fully retained and continue to be associated with the user's ID. According to the device management policy established by Guoxin Pan, even if a user changes devices, their historical health records should maintain continuity and integrity.
D. The old wristband and all its associated historical health data should be completely deleted from the system. This is to protect user privacy and ensure that there are no data residue risks when the device is refurbished and used by the next user. This decision was proposed by Project Security Lead Weihua Zhang at the privacy compliance review meeting in early September.
gold: C. The old wristband should be unbound from the user, but all historical health data generated by this wristband must be fully retained and continue to be associated with the user's ID. Hey, Assistant, quickly help me look something up. I'm working on the online consultation drug delivery status query function. The new third-party courier API we integrated is incredibly slow during testing, sometimes taking over ten seconds to respond. Users get stuck, and the experience is really bad. I vaguely remember we've encountered similar issues with slow external APIs before, right? I feel like there should be a standard way to handle this. What was the solution we decided on back then?

Options:
A. The optimization should be done from the front-end user experience side. According to the technical conventions previously established by Yu Lu and Guoxin Pan, for slow response issues with external dependencies that cannot be optimized, the standard practice is for the front-end to immediately display a transitional state and obtain the final result through backend polling, rather than making the user passively wait.
B. The current express delivery service provider should be immediately evaluated and replaced. Although Yu Lu proposed a front-end optimization plan during the discussion on October 16, it was only a temporary measure for payment channels. Project Manager Peng Sun has since clarified that for core business dependencies, the fundamental solution is to prioritize suppliers with better performance.
C. C. Message queues should be used for asynchronous decoupling. According to the latest technical selection guide released by Architect Guoxin Pan on October 20, all external API calls with response times exceeding 3 seconds must be changed to an asynchronous processing mode: the frontend sends the request to the message queue and returns immediately, and the backend consumer service processes and updates the data status. This is the final architectural principle formulated after reviewing the payment delay issue.
D. The backend team should build a caching layer. Peng Sun proposed at a previous performance review meeting that caching should be added for all third-party interfaces to reduce latency caused by repeated queries. This solution has already been written into the backend development specifications to address such performance bottlenecks.
gold: A. The optimization should be done from the front-end user experience side. According to the technical conventions previously established by Yu Lu and Guoxin Pan, for slow response issues with external dependencies that cannot be optimized, the standard practice is for the front-end to immediately display a transitional state and obtain the final result through backend polling, rather than making the user passively wait.

query:
Xiao Zhu, I've just taken over chronic disease management. I want to ask about the 'Medication Reminder' feature. How should we store the time set by the user on the backend? I've seen some people suggest storing the user's local time directly, while others say to convert it to the server's timezone. Does our project have a unified standard for this? I'm worried about getting it wrong.

Options:
A. A more robust solution should be adopted: simultaneously storing the UTC timestamp and a field representing the user's original time zone offset. This new specification was determined by Li Jin and the architecture team at the technical review meeting on October 20, aiming to solve the daylight saving time switching issue for international users and ensure that the user's original setting time can be accurately restored under any circumstances.

Xiao A, please help me out quickly. The product team just brought in a new batch of "smart temperature patches" and asked me to quickly come up with a test plan for integration. I'm swamped with a ton of things right now and really don't have time to go through previous meeting minutes. I remember our team had a set of recognized testing priorities for this kind of IoT hardware, right? What were they? What aspects should I prioritize?

Options:
A. The focus should be on testing the device's power consumption and user experience. According to the latest "V3.2 Hardware Admission Requirements" released by the Product Department, considering the long-term wear characteristics of the temperature patch, battery life and the comfort of imperceptible wear are key business indicators determining whether it can be launched.
B. Security and high concurrency performance should be the primary test points. Mingzhi Li emphasized at the security special meeting on November 5 that, given recent data breaches by competitors, all new device connections must pass complete penetration and stress tests. He requested Qingni Jiang to update the testing framework, making encrypted transmission and the responsiveness of 10,000 concurrent users the highest priority.
C. Priority should be given to connection stability, data transmission latency, and anomaly handling. According to the standards set by Mingzhi Li for real IoT device interaction testing, these three are the core requirements to ensure the access quality of all IoT devices, and Qingni Jiang's subsequent tests also strictly followed this practice.
D. D. Prioritize evaluating the accuracy and compliance of data collection. According to Qingni Jiang's conclusions at the test review meeting on November 4, there was a slight drift in the previous blood glucose meter data. Therefore, for new devices, data calibration and privacy compliance must be the primary testing tasks.
gold: C. Priority should be given to connection stability, data transmission latency, and anomaly handling. According to the standards set by Mingzhi Li for real IoT device interaction testing, these three are the core requirements to ensure the access quality of all IoT devices, and Qingni Jiang's subsequent tests also strictly followed this practice.

I just met with Lei Wang, and he suggested we package the desensitized user data and send it to our AI partner for joint modeling. He thinks this could save us a lot of R&D time. Options:
A. This proposal is generally feasible, but directly packaging and sending the data carries too much risk. We should adopt a 'data sandbox' approach, allowing partner organizations to access data and train models within our controlled environment, ensuring data never leaves our domain. This way, we can leverage external computing power while guaranteeing data security and control, which is a common collaboration model in the industry.
B. This proposal is not feasible. According to the principles established by Weihua Zhang on January 31, "The Final Report on Compliance Research in the Healthcare Industry" is the "fundamental law" for all our technical development. Providing user health data (even if de-identified) to any third-party organization carries extremely high compliance risks and severely violates the core principles of data security and privacy protection outlined in that report.
C. Can be executed. Boss Zhang explicitly stated at the AI Collaboration Special Meeting on February 10 that to accelerate technological breakthroughs, data cooperation with top research institutions that have passed security certification is permitted. As long as we use the latest differential privacy technology to perform secondary desensitization on the data and have the legal department review the cooperation agreement, we can initiate joint modeling. This move is considered a key step in promoting the intelligent upgrade of our online diagnosis and treatment system.
D. In principle, yes, but only after special approval from the Project Data Security Committee. Product Manager Lei Wang must lead the effort to prepare a detailed explanation of the data usage scope and a data anonymization plan, and sign a supplementary Data Confidentiality Agreement with the partner organization. As long as the process is compliant and approval is granted, it can be executed.

query:
Our health records system has received a deletion request from an important user. Our legal department requires us to completely erase all traces of this user from our system, especially ensuring that all data they previously contributed is permanently removed from all historical versions of the AI chronic disease prediction model. Please have the technical team evaluate this and provide the operational steps.

Options:
A. This issue has been resolved. At the technical architecture meeting on February 15, chaired by Mingzhi Li, we decided to introduce the 'Model Data Reverse Mapping' tool. This tool can reverse-index a user's anonymized data slices in historical models based on their user ID and perform physical erasure. I have asked Engineer Wang to prepare the execution script. Please send him the user's ID, and the operation can be completed within 2 hours.
B. Feasible. We need to activate the 'Data Contamination Traceability' emergency plan, roll back the training batches containing this user's data, and retrain the affected historical models. This process requires cooperation between the DBA and algorithm teams, is estimated to take 5 working days, and will temporarily affect the availability of the model repository.
C. Completely deleting historical data is too risky. According to data governance regulations, we should adopt a 'logical deletion' approach: mark the user data as 'invalid' in the model metadata, and automatically skip this data using a filter when subsequently calling historical models for inference or analysis. This approach satisfies compliance requirements while ensuring the integrity of historical models.
D. Based on the technical pre-research conclusions, we are unable to fully trace and delete this user's anonymized data from historical training models. This is technically extremely difficult and costly. The correct compliance action is to immediately physically delete or strongly encrypt and isolate all of this user's Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and ensure that their data will not be used for any future model training or data analysis.
gold: D. Based on the technical pre-research conclusions, we are unable to fully trace and delete this user's anonymized data from historical training models. This is technically extremely difficult and costly. The correct compliance action is to immediately physically delete or strongly encrypt and isolate all of this user's Personally Identifiable Information (PII), and ensure that their data will not be used for any future model training or data analysis.

query:
Ugh, this online consultation project is really pushing us. To make debugging and troubleshooting easier later on, I'm planning to log user inquiries and doctor replies from the "Doctor-Patient Communication" module directly to the logging platform in plain text. This would be the fastest way to pinpoint issues; we can't go digging through the database every time, that's too inefficient. I think this solution is viable, there shouldn't be any pitfalls, right?

Options:
A. Using a third-party logging platform might be too costly. Based on the feedback from previous technical review meetings, we recommend using the company's in-house ELK cluster to store these logs. This approach will not only meet the need for fast indexing but also effectively control the budget and unify the technology stack.
B. This solution involves sensitive data and requires approval from the security department. Please first draft a detailed technical proposal and submit it to Weihua Zhang, the security lead, for evaluation. He will provide the final opinion based on data de-identification and access control policies.
C. Storing in plaintext is too risky. According to the resolution from the architecture upgrade meeting chaired by Jianguo Huang on February 25, such sensitive data should be stored in the logging system after applying 'Field-Level Encryption'. We can use the company's encryption service to encrypt critical fields, and then a specific service can decrypt them during queries. This ensures security without affecting query efficiency for most scenarios.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the non-functional requirements baseline established for the project, the system's data storage must strictly comply with HIPAA requirements. Storing sensitive information, such as consultation records containing patient identity and medical conditions, in plain text on a logging platform would directly violate this regulation, posing serious data security and compliance risks.

query:
Xiao Zhu, we need to prioritize the health record permission feature. I'm thinking that to speed things up, we shouldn't build a separate authorization center service for now; it's too much work. Let's integrate the permission and role management logic directly into the existing user service to get it running, and we can refactor it later. Could you double-check for me? I don't recall any particular limitations, right? No one has ever objected to doing it this way, have they?

Options:
A. Consider integrating a third-party IDaaS service (e.g., Auth0) instead of in-house development. Mingzhi Li previously mentioned in a tech-sharing session that for common capabilities like authentication, we can evaluate mature external solutions to improve efficiency, which allows for faster deployment and compliance with industry security standards.
B. This solution is feasible and has been confirmed. At the architecture review meeting last Wednesday (February 26), Huilan Chen and Mingzhi Li jointly decided that to accelerate the launch of version 1.0, the authorization logic would be temporarily coupled within the user service, and the Facade pattern would be used to reserve interfaces. The plan is to split the services in version 2.0. The relevant meeting minutes have already been distributed.
C. This plan is not feasible. According to the architectural principles previously established by Huilan Chen, an independent authorization center service is the cornerstone of our health record product. It must be built independently from the outset to ensure user data security and privacy, and this cannot be compromised for the sake of progress.
D. Feasible in principle, this is a common agile development strategy. However, it must be confirmed with Guoxin Pan, as his product analysis report may involve long-term data isolation requirements. If he agrees, we can proceed, but a refactor must be scheduled for the next quarter.
gold: C. This plan is not feasible. According to the architectural principles previously established by Huilan Chen, an independent authorization center service is the cornerstone of our health record product. It must be built independently from the outset to ensure user data security and privacy, and this cannot be compromised for the sake of progress.

query:
Xiao A, the product team is really pushing hard for the 'Medication Reminder' feature for the online consultation project. They want to see a prototype by next week. I've looked into it, and if we stick to the old Java stack, the development cycle will be too long. I'm planning to go directly with Vue3 and Python. This combination is perfect for handling scheduled tasks and message pushes, and I can get it done in a week. No one should object, right? I'm going to start working on it directly. Could you please double-check it for me to avoid any issues later?

Options:
A. A. Using Vue for the frontend is acceptable, but the backend should be standardized. The PoC analysis previously conducted by Huihong Fu showed that while Python has advantages in certain scenarios, considering unified operations and maintenance and the team's technical expertise, it was ultimately decided that all business backends must use Java, except for special data analysis tasks.
B. Your proposal complies with the latest specifications. Mingzhi Li updated the technical guidelines at the architecture committee review meeting in early March. To promote a more flexible microservices strategy, newly developed independent functional modules are recommended to use a lightweight technology stack. The meeting minutes specifically noted that Vue3 and Python (FastAPI) are the preferred combination, and this resolution has been synchronized to the project knowledge base.
C. This solution does not meet the project's technical specifications. According to the final decision on technology stack selection announced by Mingzhi Li, the person in charge, all front-end development should use React and back-end development should use Java + Spring Boot to ensure the project's technical consistency and long-term maintainability.
D. Feasible in principle. Although the project's main technology stack is Java, Junxin Yuan, the technical lead, mentioned in the weekly meeting that for independent, non-core microservices like "Medication Reminder," they could pilot more efficient technology stacks such as Python, provided the solution passes the architecture review.
gold: C. This solution does not meet the project's technical specifications. According to the final decision on technology stack selection announced by Mingzhi Li, the person in charge, all front-end development should use React and back-end development should use Java + Spring Boot to ensure the project's technical consistency and long-term maintainability.

AI, the new backend is launching soon, and time is really tight. I'm responsible for the 'Partner Institution Management' module, and for the 'Partner Hospital List' API, I plan to just return all the data in one go. I see there aren't many hospital records right now, and this way, the frontend will be easier to handle, and I can develop faster, avoiding the hassle of pagination. I think this is settled. I'm about to submit a CR. Could you please double-check it for me? There shouldn't be any issues, right?

Options:
A. Yes. Product Manager Huilan Chen confirmed at the requirements review meeting on March 8 that the 'Partner Institution Management' module, as a backend configuration function, has few users and low concurrency. To facilitate rapid iteration, its list interface can temporarily forgo pagination. Pagination will be reconsidered and refactored later, depending on data growth.
B. The plan is feasible. Considering that the frequency of changes for this type of basic data is low, a full return can be adopted. At the performance optimization special meeting on March 10, architect Feng Zhou suggested that for fixed lists with data volumes less than 1000, the strategy of full return plus front-end caching should be prioritized to reduce server-side pressure.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to the architectural specifications previously emphasized by Technical Lead Mingzhi Li, all list-type interfaces in the online medical consultation service system must support paginated queries. This is a unified requirement, regardless of the current data volume. Please modify your interface design according to the specifications.
D. This solution complies with the latest specifications. At the Q1 architecture review and debrief meeting on March 15, Mingzhi Li explicitly pointed out that to enhance front-end flexibility and reduce the aggregation complexity of the BFF layer, for non-core backend management lists with data entities smaller than 1KB and a predictable total number, a one-time full load should be prioritized. Your 'cooperating hospital list' perfectly fits this scenario and can be implemented directly.
gold: C. This solution is not feasible. According to the architectural specifications previously emphasized by Technical Lead Mingzhi Li, all list-type interfaces in the online medical consultation service system must support paginated queries. This is a unified requirement, regardless of the current data volume. Please modify your interface design according to the specifications.

query:
AI, please double-check this for me. The online consultation project is on a tight deadline. The PRD for the doctor's end needs to be approved this Friday, and I'm running out of time. I plan to finish writing the core features like consultation and e-prescriptions and hand them over to development so they can get started. As for the doctor qualification verification, the logic is too complex, so I plan to push it to the next iteration for refinement. This should save a lot of time, right?

Options:
A. This arrangement works. At yesterday afternoon's project progress review meeting, Jianguo Huang already agreed that to accelerate the launch of version 1.0, non-core transaction path features like doctor onboarding review can be postponed. He instructed operations to temporarily support this with manual review, and to plan the systematic solution for version 1.1. So, you can now focus on writing the PRD for core functionalities.
B. Yes, that's fine. Considering the project schedule, I suggest you first reserve sections in the PRD for the review process and qualification requirements, and briefly describe the core logic in one or two sentences. Then, when the core features are being developed, you can use that time window to refine this part of the document. This way, it won't block development and also leaves room for design.
C. This arrangement is inappropriate. According to Jianguo Huang's previous request, the PRD for the doctor-side features must clearly define the review process and qualification requirements, as the operations team needs this information to configure the backend. Omitting this will block downstream work, so it cannot be postponed to the next iteration.
D. This arrangement is reasonable. According to the division of labor, the product team should focus on core user flows. Specific rules for doctor qualification verification should be formulated by the operations team and provided to development. You can state "Verification logic to be defined by operations" in the PRD and then circulate the document to them.
gold: C. This arrangement is inappropriate. According to Jianguo Huang's previous request, the PRD for the doctor-side features must clearly define the review process and qualification requirements, as the operations team needs this information to configure the backend. Omitting this will block downstream work, so it cannot be postponed to the next iteration.
